newsitem.title: USA: Oglethorpe Power splits into 3 business units.
newsitem.headline: Oglethorpe Power splits into 3 business units.

text.p: Georgia-based Oglethorpe Power Corp said Tuesday it has divided its business into three separate operating companies in a move to better position itself for the full deregulation of the U.S. utility industry.

Oglethorpe, the nation's largest supply cooperative measured in assets, customers and power sales, will split its operations into power generation, transmission and system operations, the company said in a statement.
Each unit will have its owns management and board of directors.

"This restructuring effectively aligns our business with developing regulatory and industry trends and will result in greater flexibility and, ultimately, better service to our 39 member systems and the 2.6 million Georgians they serve," Tom Kilgore, Oglethorpe president and CEO said.
The transmission business will be owned and operated by a newly-formed electric membership corporation called Georgia Transmission Corp.
A not-for-profit corporation named Georgia System Operations Corp will handle the systems operations side of the business.
Oglethorpe Power will continue to own and operate its existing power plants. The company owns or leases plants with an overall generating capacity of 3,338 megawatts.
All 39 member systems out of a total of Georgia's 42 customer-owned Electric Membersip Corporations (EMCs), will be members of the three operating companies, Oglethorpe said.
Also aimed at restructuring its business, Oglethorpe over the past several months has signed two agreements to supply Oglethorpe's long-term, system-wide power requirements.
The first, negotiated in November with LG&E Power Marketing, calls for the LG&E Energy unit to provide about 200 million megawatt hours of power to Oglethorpe over the next 15 years.
The second, signed with Morgan Stanley Capital Corp late last month, is expected to have a term of up to eight years and cover up to half of Oglethorpe's power requirements.
